title: Web Development · Chapter 2
description: Markup languages and HTML: presentation layer, HTML history and XHTML, tags and structure, lists, links, images, tables, forms, semantic tags, media and entities.

topics.title: 2.1 Presentation Layer
topics.description: What the presentation layer is and the roles of HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

questions.prompt: What is the presentation layer?

options.text: The database that stores a website's data
The cables that carry internet traffic
The server that runs PHP code
The part users access through a browser, made of UI components and UI process components

questions.explanation: The presentation layer is what users see and interact with in the browser.

questions.prompt: Which three core technologies are used to build the presentation layer? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: HTML (content), CSS (look) and JavaScript (interactivity).

questions.prompt: Which technology determines WHAT your website will contain?
questions.explanation: HTML = content and structure; CSS = how it looks; JavaScript = how it behaves.

questions.prompt: Which technology controls how a website LOOKS?
questions.explanation: CSS controls presentation: colours, fonts, layout.

questions.prompt: Which technology makes a website interactive — responsive to a user's actions?
questions.explanation: JavaScript (and its frameworks) handles interactivity.

questions.prompt: Which JavaScript frameworks/libraries are named in your notes for making pages dynamic? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Angular and React. MySQL is a database; Apache is a web server.

topics.title: 2.2 Markup Languages & HTML History
topics.description: What a markup language is, examples, W3C/WHATWG, Tim Berners-Lee and HTML versions.

questions.prompt: What is a markup language?

options.text: A language that performs calculations and logic
A language that annotates text so a computer can manipulate (format and align) it

questions.explanation: A markup language labels content so it can be formatted and laid out.

questions.prompt: How is a markup language different from a programming language?

options.text: It runs faster than a programming language
It labels (marks up) content to define its role and layout instead of executing logical instructions
It can only be used on servers

questions.explanation: Markup doesn't execute logic — it simply marks up raw content such as text, images and links.

questions.prompt: HTML is a programming language.
questions.explanation: HTML is a markup language: it describes content, it doesn't run logic like loops or calculations.

questions.prompt: Most markup languages are human-readable because they are tag-based.
questions.explanation:
Tags like

separate the markup from the text, so people can read it.

questions.prompt: Which of these are markup languages? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: HTML, XML, XHTML and LaTeX are markup languages. JavaScript and Python are programming languages.

questions.prompt: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML = HyperText Markup Language.

questions.prompt: Which organisation is regarded as the de facto body that governs HTML?
questions.explanation: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C). WHATWG formed later because W3C was slow.

questions.prompt: What does W3C stand for?
questions.explanation: W3C = World Wide Web Consortium.

questions.prompt: Why was WHATWG formed?

options.text: To build the first web browser
Because web standards were developing too slowly under W3C

questions.explanation: WHATWG (Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group) formed in response to W3C's slow progress.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, which HTML version (2018) is the latest, developed by W3C and WHATWG?
questions.explanation: Your notes say HTML 5.2 (2018). Good to know: since 2019 HTML has been maintained by WHATWG as the “HTML Living Standard”, which is updated continuously instead of getting version numbers.

questions.prompt: Who initially developed HTML in late 1991?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee designed HTML as a standard language for creating documents on the WWW. (Brendan Eich created JavaScript; Håkon Wium Lie proposed CSS.)

questions.prompt: HTML 4.01 (Dec 1999) syntax is defined using…
questions.explanation: HTML 4.01 → SGML. XHTML 1.0 → XML.

questions.prompt: XHTML 1.0 (Jan 2000) syntax is defined using…
questions.explanation: XHTML is HTML defined as an XML application.

questions.prompt: What does SGML stand for?
questions.explanation: SGML = Standard Generalized Markup Language.

questions.prompt: According to the version table, in which year was HTML5 officially released?
questions.explanation: HTML5: draft in 2008, released in 2014.

questions.prompt: Which list of HTML versions is in the correct order?
questions.explanation: 1990 HTML, 1995 HTML 2.0, 1997 HTML 3.0, Dec 1999 HTML 4.01, Jan 2000 XHTML 1.0, 2014 HTML5.

topics.title: 2.2 XHTML vs HTML
topics.description: What XHTML is and its stricter rules for documents, elements and attributes.

questions.prompt: What does XHTML stand for?
questions.explanation: XHTML = EXtensible HyperText Markup Language.

questions.prompt: Which statements about XHTML are true? (select all that apply)

options.text: It is almost identical to HTML
It is HTML written as XML
It is supported by all major browsers
It is more relaxed than HTML

questions.explanation: XHTML is HTML defined as an XML application, and it is stricter.

questions.prompt: What are the primary differences between HTML 4.01 and XHTML 1.0? (select all that apply)

options.text: XHTML element and attribute names must be lowercase
HTML requires every attribute value to be quoted
HTML allows some tags to be omitted (e.g. end tags); XHTML doesn't
XHTML requires attribute values to be quoted

questions.explanation: HTML is case-insensitive and lets you skip some end tags; XHTML is lowercase, quoted and always closed.

questions.prompt: Which are MANDATORY in an XHTML document? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: DOCTYPE, xmlns on <html>, and html/head/title/body are all required.

questions.prompt: Which are rules for XHTML ELEMENTS? (select all that apply)

options.text: The document must have one root element
Elements may overlap if the browser can understand them

questions.explanation: Proper nesting, always closed, lowercase, one root element.

questions.prompt: Which are rules for XHTML ATTRIBUTES? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Lowercase names, quoted values, no minimization.

questions.prompt: “Attribute minimization is forbidden” in XHTML. Which line is valid XHTML?
questions.explanation: Minimised attributes like `checked` must be written in full (checked="checked"), quoted, lowercase, and the empty element closed with />.

questions.prompt: Which line is valid XHTML?
questions.explanation: Lowercase, properly nested, and every element closed.

questions.prompt: How must an empty element like a line break be written in XHTML?
questions.explanation:
In XHTML every element must be closed, so empty elements self-close:
. (Plain HTML5 also accepts
.)

questions.prompt:
In HTML (not XHTML), element names are case-insensitive, so

and

mean the same thing.
questions.explanation: HTML names are case-insensitive; XHTML requires lowercase.

questions.prompt: XHTML 1.0 requires this attribute on the <html> element. Which is it?
questions.explanation: The XML namespace attribute: <html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">.

topics.title: 2.3–2.4 Tags, Elements & Basic Structure
topics.description: Start/end tags, DOCTYPE, html/head/title/body, the modern boilerplate, headings, paragraphs and nesting.

questions.prompt: In HTML, what counts as a tag?

options.text: Any line ending with a semicolon

questions.explanation: Any string of the form < … > is a tag.

questions.prompt: How do you recognise an END tag?
questions.explanation: End tags begin with ). All other tags are start tags.

questions.prompt: In the start tag below, what is the element name?
questions.explanation: The string at the beginning of a start/end tag is the element name. `class` is an attribute and `intro` its value.

questions.prompt: Look at the tag below. Which statements are correct? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Element name first, then attribute name="value" pairs.

questions.prompt: Write the document type declaration for an HTML5 page.
questions.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> goes on the very first line. It is not case-sensitive.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of <!DOCTYPE>?

options.text: To tell the browser which HTML or XHTML version and type the document uses

questions.explanation: The DOCTYPE tells the browser which version of HTML/XHTML to expect.

questions.prompt: The root element of an HTML document must be <html>.
questions.explanation: Everything else sits inside <html>.

questions.prompt: What do the <html> and </html> tags indicate?

options.text: The start and end of the visible content
The start and end of an HTML document

questions.explanation: They wrap the entire document.

questions.prompt: Which element contains the information displayed in the browser's client area (the visible page)?
questions.explanation: Visible content goes in <body>.

questions.prompt: Which of these belong inside <head>? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: <head> holds information used by the browser: title, meta, styles, scripts. Headings and footers are visible content → <body>.

questions.prompt: Where does the text inside <title> appear?

options.text: In the browser's title bar / tab
At the bottom of the page
As the biggest heading on the page
Nowhere — it is only a comment

questions.explanation: The title shows in the title bar or tab (and in bookmarks).

questions.prompt: Besides <!DOCTYPE>, four sets of tags define a page's structure: <html>, <head>, <______> and <body>. Fill in the blank.
questions.explanation: The four sets are html, head, title and body.

questions.prompt: Which skeleton is correctly structured?
questions.explanation: <head> comes first and closes before <body> opens; both sit inside <html>.

questions.prompt: In the modern boilerplate, what does this line do?

options.text: Makes the page responsive on phones
Sets the character encoding so all characters (e.g. é, ©, emojis) display correctly
Sets the page language to English

questions.explanation: charset="UTF-8" sets the character encoding.

questions.prompt: In the modern boilerplate, what does this line do?

options.text: Makes the page use the device's width so it displays properly on mobile
Prevents the page from being zoomed in a desktop browser

questions.explanation: Without the viewport meta tag, phones render the page at desktop width and shrink it.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of lang="en" on <html lang="en">?

options.text: It declares the page's language (helps screen readers, translation and search engines)
It is required for CSS to work
It makes the page load faster

questions.explanation: The lang attribute declares the content language.

questions.prompt: In the boilerplate, where is the <script src="script.js"> tag placed, and why?

options.text: Just before </body>, so the HTML loads before the script runs

questions.explanation: Placing scripts at the end of <body> lets the page content load first.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct way to write an HTML comment?
questions.explanation: HTML comments use <!-- -->. /* */ is a CSS comment and // is a JavaScript comment.

questions.prompt: What does © display on the page?
questions.explanation: © is the HTML entity for the copyright symbol, used in the boilerplate footer.

questions.prompt: Which heading tag produces the LARGEST heading?
questions.explanation: Headings go from <h1> (largest/most important) to <h6> (smallest).

questions.prompt: How many heading levels does HTML have?
questions.explanation: Six: <h1> to <h6>.

questions.prompt: Which tag defines a paragraph?
questions.explanation:
…

defines a paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which snippet is correctly nested?
questions.explanation:
Tags must close in the reverse order they were opened. Overlapping tags such as

are wrong.

questions.prompt: This snippet is correctly nested.
questions.explanation:
closes before

, so the tags overlap. Close the inner element first:

…

then .

questions.prompt: How are most HTML markup tags used?

options.text: In pairs: an opening tag and a closing tag
Always alone with no closing tag

questions.explanation:
Most tags come in pairs, like

…

. A few (e.g. ,
) are empty elements with no closing tag.

topics.title: 2.5 Lists, Links & Images
topics.description: Ordered, unordered and description lists; ; ; plus useful extras.

questions.prompt: Which tag creates a list whose items are marked with NUMBERS?
questions.explanation: <ol> = ordered list (numbers).

questions.prompt: Which tag creates a list whose items are marked with BULLETS?
questions.explanation: <ul> = unordered list (bullets).

questions.prompt: In <ol> and <ul>, which tag starts each list item?
questions.explanation: Each item is an <li>.

questions.prompt: In a description list, which tag DESCRIBES the term?
questions.explanation: <dl> wraps the list, <dt> is the term (name), <dd> describes it.

questions.prompt: In a description list, which tag holds the TERM (name)?
questions.explanation: <dt> = description term.

questions.prompt: Which output does this code produce?
questions.code:
<dl>
  <dt>Langkawi</dt>
    <dd>Island in Kedah</dd>
  <dt>Cameron Highlands</dt>
    <dd>Hill station in Pahang</dd>
  <dt>Melaka</dt>
    <dd>Historical city</dd>
</dl>

image.alt: Bulleted list: Langkawi, Cameron Highlands, Melaka
Numbered list: 1. Langkawi, 2. Cameron Highlands, 3. Melaka
Each place name on its own line with an indented description below it

questions.explanation: <dl> shows each <dt> term with its <dd> description indented underneath — no numbers or bullets.

questions.prompt: Which output does this code produce?

image.alt: Each place name on its own line with an indented description below it
Numbered list: 1. Langkawi, 2. Cameron Highlands, 3. Melaka
Bulleted list: Langkawi, Cameron Highlands, Melaka

questions.explanation: <ol> numbers its items 1, 2, 3.

questions.prompt: How do you make an ordered list count with capital letters (A, B, C)?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. The type attribute on <ol> can be 1, A, a, I or i. start="5" starts counting at 5 and reversed counts down.

questions.prompt: You can nest a list by putting a <ul> inside an <li>.
questions.explanation:
Extra — not in your notes. Sub-lists go inside a list item:
  • Fruits
    • Apple
    • .

questions.prompt: Which tag defines a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The anchor tag <a> defines a hyperlink. (<link> connects files such as CSS in <head>.)

questions.prompt: Which attribute of <a> specifies the link's destination?
questions.explanation: href holds the URL the link points to.

questions.prompt: What does this link do when clicked?

options.text: Opens nextpage.html; the visible clickable text is “Next page”
Shows the URL as text but doesn't link anywhere
Downloads an image called Next page

questions.explanation: href = destination; the text between and is what the user clicks.

questions.prompt: What does target="_blank" do on a link?

options.text: Opens the link in the same tab
Opens the link in a new tab or window

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. target="_blank" opens a new tab/window.

questions.prompt: Which link jumps to the element with id="contact" on the same page?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. A # followed by an id links to that spot on the page (the URL's anchor).

questions.prompt: Which link opens the user's email app?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. mailto: starts an email; tel: starts a phone call on phones.

questions.prompt: Which tag displays an image?
questions.explanation: Images use .

questions.prompt: Which attribute gives the location (URL) of the image file?
questions.explanation: src = source of the image.

questions.prompt: What is the alt attribute of for?

options.text: The image's caption shown below it
Alternate text shown if the image can't be found (and read aloud by screen readers)

questions.explanation: If the browser can't load the image it shows the alt text. Screen readers read it to blind users.

questions.prompt: needs a closing tag, like .
questions.explanation: is an empty (void) element — it has no closing tag. In XHTML you write .

questions.prompt: Which line correctly sets an image to display 300 pixels wide?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. width and height attributes take a number of pixels (no unit). CSS can also set width.

topics.title: 2.5 Tables
topics.description: <table>, <tr>, <td>, <th>, borders, plus captions, row/column spans and table sections.

questions.prompt: A table is divided into ROWS with which tag?
questions.explanation: <tr> = table row.

questions.prompt: Each row is divided into data cells (columns) with which tag?
questions.explanation: <td> = table data cell.

questions.prompt: What does <td> stand for?
questions.explanation: td = table data.

questions.prompt: Which tag creates a HEADER cell (bold and centred by default)?
questions.explanation: <th> = table header cell.

questions.prompt: What can a <td> cell contain? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: A <td> can contain text, links, images, lists, forms and even other tables — but rows belong in a table, not straight inside a cell.

questions.prompt: How many ROWS does this table have (including the header row)?
questions.explanation: Three <tr> elements = three rows (1 header row + 2 data rows).

questions.prompt: How many COLUMNS does this table have?
questions.explanation: Each row has three cells, so three columns.

questions.prompt: What does border="1" do in this table?

options.text: Draws a 1-pixel border around the table and its cells

questions.explanation: border="1" turns on borders. In modern HTML you'd usually use CSS instead: border: 1px solid; plus border-collapse: collapse.

questions.prompt: The top cell in this table stretches across all three columns. Which attribute does that?

image.alt: A table whose top cell, 'Holiday Destinations', stretches across all three columns. Below it are headers Destination, Location, Type and a row Langkawi, Kedah, Island.

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <th colspan="3">Holiday Destinations</th> makes one cell span 3 columns. rowspan does the same vertically.

questions.prompt: What does rowspan="2" on a cell do?

options.text: Makes the cell stretch down across 2 rows
Makes the cell stretch across 2 columns

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. rowspan merges vertically; colspan merges horizontally.

questions.prompt: Which tag gives a table a title, shown above it?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <caption> goes straight after <table>. (<legend> is the caption for a form <fieldset>.)

questions.prompt: Which tags group parts of a table? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <thead> holds header rows, <tbody> the main rows, <tfoot> totals/footer rows.

topics.title: 2.5 Forms
topics.description: Extra — your notes list forms but don't describe them. <form>, inputs, labels, select, textarea, buttons.

questions.prompt: What is an HTML <form> used for?

options.text: Collecting user input and sending it to a server

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Forms gather input (logins, searches, sign-ups) and submit it.

questions.prompt: What does the action attribute of <form> specify?

options.text: The URL where the form data is sent

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. action="/register" sends the data to /register.

questions.prompt: Which are the two common values of the form's method attribute? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. GET and POST.

questions.prompt: Which method should a login form use to send a password?

options.text: POST — the data goes in the request body, not the URL
GET — the data is added to the URL

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. GET puts data in the URL (visible, bookmarked, logged). POST sends it in the request body. Use GET for searches, POST for sensitive or data-changing forms.

questions.prompt: Which input type hides the characters as the user types?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. password shows dots. hidden isn't shown at all — it sends a value the user doesn't see.

questions.prompt: Which of these are real <input> types? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Others include text, password, file, range, color, tel, url, search, submit, reset and hidden. A dropdown is <select>.

questions.prompt: The user must choose exactly ONE option (e.g. Male / Female). Which input type?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Radio buttons allow one choice per group. Group them by giving them the same name attribute.

questions.prompt: How do you make several radio buttons belong to one group (only one can be chosen)?

options.text: Give them all the same name attribute
Give them all the same value
Give them all the same id

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Same name = same group. ids must always be unique.

questions.prompt: The user can tick several hobbies. Which input type?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Checkboxes allow multiple selections.

questions.prompt: Which element creates a drop-down list?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <select name="state"><option>Kedah</option>…</select>.

questions.prompt: Which element creates a multi-line text box (e.g. for comments)?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <textarea rows="4" cols="40"></textarea>.

questions.prompt: What does this <label> do?

options.text: Links the text “Email” to the input with id="email", so tapping the label focuses the input
Gives the input a name for the server

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. for must match the input's id. Labels help accessibility and make small inputs easier to tap.

questions.prompt: Which attribute decides the key under which a field's value is sent to the server?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Without a name, the field's value isn't submitted. id is for labels, CSS and links.

questions.prompt: Which attribute shows grey hint text inside an empty field?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. placeholder="e.g. ali@mail.com".

questions.prompt: Which attribute stops the form submitting while a field is empty?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Add required to the input.

questions.prompt: Which create a button that submits the form? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Both submit. type="reset" clears the form instead.

questions.prompt: Which tags group related form fields and give the group a caption?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <fieldset> draws a box around the fields; <legend> is its caption.

questions.prompt: Which input type lets the user upload a file? (type="____")
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. The form also needs method="post" and enctype="multipart/form-data" to send files.

topics.title: More HTML: Semantic & Text Tags
topics.description: Extra — tags beyond your notes: header/nav/main/section/article/aside/footer, div vs span, and text formatting.

questions.prompt: Which element should wrap the main navigation links?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <nav> marks a block of navigation links.

questions.prompt: Which element holds the dominant, unique content of the page (only one visible per page)?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <main> is the page's primary content.

questions.prompt: A blog post or news story that would make sense on its own should be wrapped in…
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <article> = self-contained content.

questions.prompt: Content only loosely related to the main content, like a sidebar, belongs in…
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <aside> = sidebar / related content.

questions.prompt: A thematic group of content, normally with its own heading (e.g. “Our Services”), should use…
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <section> groups related content under a heading.

questions.prompt: Which are HTML5 semantic layout elements? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Semantic elements describe their meaning. <div> and <span> are generic containers with no meaning.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between <div> and <span>?

options.text: <div> is a block-level container; <span> is an inline container

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <div> starts on a new line and takes full width. <span> sits inside a line of text. Both are mainly hooks for CSS.

questions.prompt: Which elements are INLINE by default (they don't start a new line)? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
Extra — not in your notes.
,

, headings, lists and tables are block-level.

questions.prompt: Which tag inserts a line break?
questions.explanation:
Extra — not in your notes.
= line break.
= horizontal rule (a thematic break line).

questions.prompt: Which tag draws a horizontal line to separate sections?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <hr> = horizontal rule.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between <strong> and <b>?

options.text: <strong> means important content; <b> is only visually bold
No difference in meaning or looks

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Both look bold, but <strong> carries meaning (screen readers can stress it). Likewise <em> = emphasis vs <i> = just italic.

questions.prompt: Which tag makes the “2” in H₂O appear lowered (subscript)?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <sub> = subscript (H<sub>2</sub>O). <sup> = superscript (x<sup>2</sup>).

questions.prompt: Which tag would you use for the “2” in x² (superscript)?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <sup> raises text.

questions.prompt: Which tag highlights text like a yellow marker?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <mark> highlights.

questions.prompt: Which tag keeps all spaces and line breaks exactly as typed?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <pre> = preformatted text, shown in a monospace font. <code> marks inline code.

questions.prompt: Which tag is meant for a long quotation from another source?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <blockquote> for a block quotation; <q> for a short inline quote (adds quote marks); <cite> for a work's title.

questions.prompt: Building a whole page only with <div>s is invalid HTML.
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. It is valid, but not semantic. Semantic tags help screen readers, SEO and readability.

topics.title: More HTML: Media, Entities & Attributes
topics.description: Extra — <video>, <audio>, <iframe>, <figure>, HTML entities, global attributes and meta tags.

questions.prompt: Which tag embeds a video file?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <video src="clip.mp4" controls></video>.

questions.prompt: What does the controls attribute do on <video> or <audio>?

options.text: Shows play/pause, volume and progress controls

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. autoplay starts automatically, loop repeats, muted mutes.

questions.prompt: Which tag plays a sound file?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <audio src="song.mp3" controls>.

questions.prompt: Why put several <source> elements inside <video>?

options.text: To play several videos at once
To offer different file formats so the browser can pick one it supports

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. The browser uses the first <source> format it can play.

questions.prompt: Which tag embeds another web page inside your page (e.g. Google Maps or a YouTube player)?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. <iframe src="…">.

questions.prompt: Which pair adds an image with a caption underneath, as one unit?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. .

questions.prompt: Which HTML entity displays a less-than sign (<) as text?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. < = <, > = >, & = &, " = ",   = non-breaking space, © = ©.

questions.prompt: What does   insert?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. A space that won't break onto a new line (and isn't collapsed with other spaces).

questions.prompt: Why would you write & instead of just & in HTML?

options.text: Because & is not a valid character
It is required in every URL
Because & starts an entity, so a literal ampersand should be escaped

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. & begins entities like ©, so writing & avoids confusion.

questions.prompt: Which are GLOBAL attributes that can go on any HTML element? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. href belongs to / and src to /

questions.prompt: The same id value can be used on several elements on one page.
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. An id must be unique on the page. Use a class for something repeated.

questions.prompt: What does the title attribute do, e.g. <abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>?

options.text: Shows a tooltip with extra information when hovering
Sets the page's title bar text

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. title gives advisory text, usually shown as a tooltip.

questions.prompt: What is <meta name="description" content="…"> used for?

options.text: The text displayed at the top of the page
A short summary of the page, often shown by search engines under the link

questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Search engines may show it in results.

questions.prompt: Which line adds a small icon (favicon) to the browser tab?
questions.explanation: Extra — not in your notes. Favicons are linked in <head> with rel="icon".
